name: Tally stick
desc: Notched bones and sticks used to record counts, the earliest known aids to calculation.

name: Abacus
desc: A frame or board of movable counters for fast arithmetic, used from Sumer to modern Asia.

name: Quipu

name: Counting rods
desc: Small rods laid out on a board for place-value arithmetic in ancient China.

name: Euclidean algorithm
desc: A step-by-step procedure for the greatest common divisor, among the oldest algorithms still in use.

name: Antikythera mechanism
desc: A Greek geared device that computed astronomical positions and eclipses, the oldest known analog computer.

name: Scytale
desc: A rod around which a strip was wound to encipher messages by transposition.

name: Caesar cipher
desc: A substitution cipher shifting each letter a fixed number of places.

name: Frequency analysis

name: Vigenère cipher
desc: A polyalphabetic cipher using a keyword, long considered unbreakable.

name: Logarithm

name: Napier's bones

name: Slide rule
desc: An analog calculator of sliding logarithmic scales, the engineer's tool until the 1970s.

name: Mechanical calculator
desc: Geared machines that add and subtract automatically, starting with Schickard's calculating clock.

name: Pascaline
desc: Blaise Pascal's geared adding machine with automatic carry.

name: Leibniz wheel

name: Stepped reckoner
desc: Leibniz's calculator able to add, subtract, multiply and divide.

name: Binary number system

name: Punched tape
desc: Perforated paper strips that store instructions or data, first used to control looms.

name: Arithmometer
desc: Thomas de Colmar's calculator, the first to be mass-produced and sold commercially.

name: Difference engine
desc: Babbage's machine for tabulating polynomials by the method of finite differences.

name: Analytical engine
desc: Babbage's design for a general-purpose programmable mechanical computer with a store and mill.

name: Note G
desc: Ada Lovelace's algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, often called the first published program.

name: Tide-predicting machine

name: Ball-and-disk integrator

name: One-time pad

name: Comptometer
desc: A key-driven adding machine that made rapid office calculation routine.

name: Tabulating machine

name: Keypunch

name: Unit record equipment

name: Rotor machine

name: Enigma machine

name: Drum memory
desc: A rotating magnetic cylinder used as main storage in many early computers.

name: Differential analyser
desc: Vannevar Bush's mechanical analog computer for solving differential equations.

name: Turing machine
desc: Turing's abstract model of computation that defined what can be computed.

name: Universal Turing machine

name: Lambda calculus
desc: Church's formal system of function definition and application, the root of functional programming.

name: Switching circuit theory

name: Z1

name: Bombe
desc: Electromechanical machine used at Bletchley Park to find Enigma settings.

name: Z3

name: Floating-point arithmetic

name: Atanasoff–Berry computer
desc: An early electronic digital calculator using vacuum tubes and capacitor memory.

name: Artificial neuron
desc: McCulloch and Pitts' mathematical model of a neuron as a logic unit.

name: Colossus

name: Harvard Mark I
desc: A large electromechanical computer built by IBM and Aiken, reading instructions from tape.

name: Harvard architecture
desc: A design with separate storage and pathways for instructions and data.

name: ENIAC

name: Von Neumann architecture
desc: A design where programs and data share one memory, set out in the EDVAC report.

name: Plankalkül
desc: Zuse's design for the first high-level programming language.

name: Merge sort

name: Memex

name: Monte Carlo method

name: Simplex algorithm
desc: Dantzig's method for linear programming, a cornerstone of operations research.

name: Williams tube

name: Delay-line memory

name: Assembly language
desc: Symbolic notation for machine instructions, translated by an assembler.

name: Stored-program computer

name: Manchester Baby
desc: The first electronic stored-program computer to run a program.

name: Information theory

name: EDSAC

name: EDVAC

name: Subroutine

name: Hamming code

name: Turing test

name: Numerical weather prediction

name: Microcode

name: Magnetic-tape data storage

name: UNIVAC I

name: Ferranti Mark 1

name: LEO

name: Whirlwind I

name: Computer chess

name: Compiler

name: Huffman coding

name: Mainframe computer

name: Speech recognition

name: Magnetic-core memory

name: Transistor computer

name: Hash table

name: Dynamic programming

name: Natural language processing

name: Light pen

name: Logic Theorist

name: Finite element method

name: Fortran

name: Image scanner

name: Computer music

name: ALGOL

name: Modem

name: Video game

name: COBOL

name: Machine learning

name: Backus–Naur form

name: Garbage collection

name: Quicksort

name: Dijkstra's algorithm

name: Computer graphics
desc: Creating and displaying images with computers.

name: Time-sharing

name: Supercomputer

name: Word processor
